label: First Cave 1 finds
note: Bedouin shepherds recovered seven scrolls. Retrospective accounts differ: late 1946–early 1947; institutional summaries commonly use 1947.

sources.title: Cave 1 manuscript list: discovery date range (secondary)

label: Eleven caves yield finds
note: Searches by Bedouin and archaeologists brought manuscripts and fragments to light; Cave 10 yielded an inscribed potsherd.

label: Cave 1 excavated
note: Archaeological excavation recovered further material, including linen textiles.

label: Caves 2–6
note: Finds included the Copper Scroll in Cave 3 and thousands of manuscript fragments in Cave 4.

label: Caves 7–10
note: Greek fragments came from Cave 7; Cave 10 yielded a single inscribed potsherd.

label: Cave 11
note: Finds included the Psalms Scroll and Temple Scroll.

label: Shrine of the Book
note: The Shrine was built to house the first seven scrolls; public exhibition began in 1965.

sources.title: Google / Israel Museum digital project launch

label: Photographs become widely accessible
note: The Biblical Archaeology Society published photographs; the Huntington Library opened its photographic security copies to scholars.

sources.title: Library of Congress: Two Thousand Years Later

label: Most official editions published
note: The IAA’s expanded editorial project had published the majority of the official editions by 2001.

label: Israel Museum scrolls online
note: Five digitized scrolls became accessible through the Israel Museum and Google partnership.

sources.title: Google / Israel Museum digital project launch

label: Leon Levy Digital Library
note: The IAA launched its library with about 5,000 images of scroll fragments.

label: “Cave 12” announcement
note: The excavation team reported storage-jar fragments and material associated with scroll storage. The designation is evidence of possible former storage, not a newly recovered written scroll.

label: New fragments announced
note: The IAA announced Greek Minor Prophets fragments from the Cave of Horror at Nahal Hever, south of Qumran. Announcement date, not the date each fragment was excavated.

sources.title: NBC report of IAA announcement (March 16, 2021; corrected March 18)

label: AI studies scribal hands
note: A handwriting study found evidence for two main scribes in the Great Isaiah Scroll. Writer identification is distinct from dating.

label: Radiocarbon meets AI dating
note: The study reports 27 valid radiocarbon dates, trains Enoch on 24 dated manuscripts and predicts dates for 135 undated scrolls. Results are probability ranges; some are older than traditional estimates. Material age is not the date a text was first composed.

label: Research remains open
note: Editorial checkpoint: dating, fragment reconstruction and imaging remain research questions. This is not an announcement of a new 2026 discovery. Small training sets, calibration and contamination constrain dating models.
